dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an m-by-n real array A, this is sqrt(sum over i in Fin m of sum over j in Fin n of (A i j)^2), namely its Frobenius norm.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines both matrix-level quantities in the conclusion: the Frobenius norms of DeltaA and A.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real vector x indexed by Fin n, this is sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of (x i)^2), namely its Euclidean norm.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For each column j, it defines the Euclidean norms of i maps to DeltaA i j and i maps to A i j in the columnwise hypothesis.

binders: For every pair of natural numbers m and n.
For every pair of real arrays A and DeltaA of shape m-by-n, represented as functions Fin m -> Fin n -> Real.
hypotheses: For every column index j in Fin n, the Euclidean norm of the column i maps to DeltaA i j is at most eta times the Euclidean norm of the column i maps to A i j.
conclusions: The Frobenius norm of DeltaA is at most eta times the Frobenius norm of A.
mathematical_definitions: For a vector x indexed by Fin m, ||x||_2 = sqrt(sum over i in Fin m of x_i^2).
For an m-by-n array B, ||B||_F = sqrt(sum over i in Fin m of sum over j in Fin n of B_ij^2).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For arbitrary finite dimensions m and n, arbitrary real m-by-n arrays A and DeltaA, and a nonnegative real eta, if every column of DeltaA has Euclidean norm at most eta times the Euclidean norm of the corresponding column of A, then the Frobenius norm of DeltaA is at most eta times the Frobenius norm of A.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimensions m and n may be zero.
If n = 0, the columnwise hypothesis is vacuous and both Frobenius norms are zero, so the conclusion is 0 <= 0.
If m = 0, every column norm and both Frobenius norms are zero; all column inequalities and the conclusion reduce to 0 <= 0.
If eta = 0, each column hypothesis forces the corresponding column of DeltaA to have zero Euclidean norm.
If a column of A has zero Euclidean norm, the corresponding hypothesis forces that column of DeltaA to have zero Euclidean norm.

The proposition assumes only columnwise norm bounds; it does not encode entrywise bounds, rowwise bounds, a construction of DeltaA, rounding behavior, a converse, equality conditions, or optimality of eta.
There are no existential witnesses or additional dimension, positivity, invertibility, or nonzero assumptions.
